REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - AUGUST 24, 2026 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
PUBLIC ADVISORY: THIS MEETING WILL BE CONDUCTED IN A HYBRID MODEL WITH BOTH IN-PERSON ATTENDANCE AND VIRTUAL PARTICIPATION.
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda packet is available at cerritos.gov and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st Floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours as posted. Materials received after posting of the agenda will also be available for public inspection. For assistance, contact the Office of the City Clerk at city_clerk@cerritos.gov or (562) 916-1248.
Order of Agenda
The City Council may reorder agenda items by majority vote of members present.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public may observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at cerritos.gov/agendas or the City’s YouTube channel , on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public comment may be provided in person, remotely via Zoom, or in writing as described below. Public comment on business agenda items will be heard during consideration of that business item. Public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and non-agenda items will be heard during Agenda Item No. 6.
Remote/teleconference (Zoom) participation :
PLEASE ENSURE YOUR ZOOM SOFTWARE IS UPDATED TO PROVIDE LIVE COMMENTS
Meeting ID: 897 8691 1692
Smart Phone or Computer (Zoom App required): https://us02web.zoom.us/j/89786911692
Phone Call-In: (669) 900-6833
To request to speak via Zoom, to join or call in at the meeting start time and use the “Raise Hand” feature or press *9 by phone during the item on which you wish to speak. Press *6 to unmute when prompted.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Written comments may be submitted by email to city_clerk@cerritos.gov or delivered to the Office of the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. Timely comments will be distributed to the legislative body and retained as part of the official record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact City of Cerritos ADA/504 Coordinator, Drew Schneider, at (562) 916-1314 at least 72 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD MONDAY,

18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA AND VIA ZOOM
TELECONFERENCE, MEETING ID# 897 8691 1692.

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Cynthia Nava, City Clerk.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by the Optimist Club of Cerritos.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jennifer Hong
  Council/Agency Member Sophia M. Tse
  Council/Agency Member Frank Aurelio Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor/Chair Lynda Provido Johnson

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  None.

5B.  An informational report and overview of the services provided by SoCalGas.

  Blake Perez, Public Affairs Manager, SoCalGas, provided an informational
  presentation. A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Sam Desai expressed appreciation to the City Council for reminding residents of the
  City’s adopted low-income water and sewer utility assistance program.

  Unidentified speaker expressed concern regarding community tax responsibility and
  stated a racial slur.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

5C.  Review and consideration of City Council appointments to the Cerritos Advisory
  Boards (Commissions and Committees) (2025-2027 Term) (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Cynthia Nava, City Clerk.
 City of Cerritos  Monday, August 24, 2026, 7:00 p.m.

5.  Presentations/Appointments (continued)

5C.  (continued)

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  David Pylman expressed support for the public’s opportunity to provide public
  comments after nominations are made, but prior to City Council action approving
  nominations to Cerritos Advisory Boards.

  Sam Desai inquired regarding oaths of office taken by Cerritos Advisory Board
  members and regarding the scope of member responsibilities.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Tse, and seconded by Yokoyama, to approve
  Councilmember Tse’s nomination listed below to serve the remainder of the 2025-
  2027 term, through April 30, 2027 (COUNCIL):

  Name  Advisory Board
  Laura Walton  Economic Development Commission

  AYES:  Hong, Tse, Yokoyama, Pulido, Johnson

  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  Jason M.V.P. Amansec  Planning Commission

  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  Cynthia Nava, City Clerk, administered the oath of office to appointee, Jason M.V.P.
  Amansec.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period for items not listed on the meeting
  agenda but that were within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the
  Consent Calendar, and Closed Session.
 City of Cerritos  Monday, August 24, 2026, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 3 of 15

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Robert Shavelle spoke regarding the Cerritos Iron-Wood Nine Golf Course and
  expressed appreciation for the related agenda report presented at the Monday, July
  27, 2027, 7 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency meeting. He also expressed support
  for potential golf course fee increases.

  David Pylman expressed support for a five-minute public speaker time limit at
  Cerritos public meetings and expressed concern regarding limitations to public
  comment time, given recent Cerritos public meeting schedule adjustments; the City’s
  Register of Demands; and public records.

  Gavin Riley expressed concern regarding the City’s codified building regulations and
  permitting process.

  Sam Desai expressed concern regarding Cerritos public meeting administration and
  public comment provisions, expressed support for a five-minute public speaker time
  limit, and requested separate consideration of Agenda Item 7E as listed on the
  meeting agenda.

  Carla Gilhuys expressed concern regarding limitations to public comment time given
  recent Cerritos public meeting schedule adjustments, and activities related to a
  public speaker at the previous City Council meeting.

  Charles Sooter expressed concern about the City’s financial position and expressed
  support for a potential increase in the City’s sales tax to help offset the City budget
  deficit and potentially reduce the impact on residents of the City’s recently adjusted
  water and sewer rates.

  Kavisha Prajapati expressed concern regarding Cerritos public meeting
  administration; activities related to a public speaker at the previous City Council
  meeting; and recent campaign activity related to local voter-initiated petitions in
  circulation and not yet filed.

  Kirit Chauhan expressed concern regarding public safety in the community.

  Grace Hu expressed opposition to the City’s purchase of real property located at
  16550 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, California 90703 (Item 7C).

  Charles Joslin expressed concern regarding Cerritos public meeting administration
  and public comment provisions and activities related to a public speaker at the
  previous City Council meeting.

  Kurtis Forsythe expressed concern regarding activities related to a public speaker at
  the previous City Council meeting and recent campaign activity related to local voter-

  the official record. (Documents submitted to the City Council at a public meeting are

7B.3. Approval of Fiscal Year 2025-26 budget amendment (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Hong, to authorize an
  administrative-initiated Fiscal Year (FY) 2025-26 budget amendment in accordance with
  Joint Budget Resolution No. 2025-19/No. CSA 2025-02 and the Strategic Financial Plan
  and Budget Preparation Policy (Policy 2.04) as adopted by the City Council, as follows:

  1. Account/Project:  110211-61120 (County Building & Safety Services –
  Expenditures) - $162,000
  110211-41110 (Building Permits - County -
  Revenues) - $574,000

(minutes continue on the next page)
 City of Cerritos  Monday, August 24, 2026, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 6 of 15

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7B.  Approval of Financial Reports (continued)

7B.3. (continued)

  Justification: A budget amendment of $162,000 is requested for the Building &
  Safety Services account to address increased expenditures resulting from a rise
  in construction/inspection activity and development projects Citywide, particularly
  in Spring/Summer 2026. The City contracts with the County of Los Angeles to
  provide Building & Safety services, including plan check and inspection services.
  These expenditures are pass-through expenses, with project applicants bearing
  the costs of these services. Due to the increase in development activity toward
  the end of Fiscal Year 2025-2026, both expenditures and revenues exceeded the
  amounts originally budgeted. In addition to the expenditure amendment, a
  budget amendment of $574,000 is requested for Revenue Account 110211-
  41110 to reflect additional revenues received during Fiscal Year 2025-2026. The
  significant increase in revenue is attributed to an increase in permit activity and
  fees. Due to the County permit fee structure for permit issuance and the fee
  structure for cost of hourly County services to the City, the City is able to offset
  the difference for any services. These amendments are fully offsetting and do not
  require the use of additional General Fund resources (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Tse, Yokoyama, Pulido, Johnson
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
